Subject: EdgeFusion on-prem cluster design review

Thanks again for the workshop this morning — really helpful. Attached is a short 'diff' of the proposed cluster topology (ef-architecture-diff.pdf) and a preliminary storage risk register for our internal review (storage-risk-register.xlsx).

Key constraints from our side:
- No outbound internet egress from the cluster other than a vetted proxy host.
- KMS must be customer-managed (HSM-backed) and not leave our VPC.
- Racks have mixed NVMe + HDD; we prefer local NVMe for model cache but need persistent volumes for user data.

Outstanding asks:
1) Confirm recommended node pool sizes for a mixed GPU+CPU profile (burst to 8 GPUs).
2) Suggested PV classes and fallback for archival to object store behind private link.
3) Network layout (BGP vs static routing for pod egress) and firewall port list for preflight.

Can Redwood produce an 'airgap bundle' and a preflight checklist we can hand to ops?

Attachments: ef-architecture-diff.pdf (diagram), storage-risk-register.xlsx (initial)

— Alex

Thanks Alex — this is a great starting point. I pulled the attachments into our shared drive and started a short checklist. A few quick confirmations and proposed decisions from Redwood's side to keep momentum: 

Decisions we recommend to lock in during preflight: 
- Network: prefer Calico with BGP (full-mesh) for pod routing where BGP is supported in your ToR; fall back to static routes if BGP is unavailable. We will include iptables/NAT egress patterns in the preflight.
- Storage: local NVMe for ephemeral model KV cache + read-through to a Ceph/iSCSI-backed PV class for persistent volumes. We'll map StorageClass names (redwood-ephemeral, redwood-pv) in the deploy manifests.
- Node pools: propose three pools — control-plane (m), gpu-burst (p4-equivalent), cpu-worker (c). I've attached nodepool-sizing.csv with initial vCPU/RAM/GPU counts and a crude cost/throughput column.

Immediate actions for EdgeFusion ops team:
- Confirm rack inventory (units with NVMe vs HDD) and per-rack power/UPS.
- Provide expected 95th percentile concurrent inference requests to size burst GPU pool.
- Identify on-prem proxy host IPs allowed for egress and the KMS endpoint IPs.

Yes — we can produce an offline 'airgap bundle' and a one-page preflight with exact firewall ports, kernel modules, and required images. We'll also provide an encrypted KMS integration doc.

I'll queue a 30-min technical preflight on Friday (your local time) to run through the checklist. Karthik — joining you to scope the exact PV binding behavior and eviction thresholds.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Adding some technical notes that should feed into the preflight doc — pulling from our private deployment playbook: 

Network / Egress
- If you run Calico with BGP, advertise pod CIDRs into the ToR and avoid SNAT for pod-to-external traffic; this reduces NAT table pressure when scaling.
- For customers that cannot expose BGP, we provide a stable SNAT gateway design (cluster-egress nodes) with hairpin rules for internal services.
- Required ports: 6443 (API), 2379-2380 (etcd if separated), 10250 (kubelet), 179 (BGP), 7946 (flannel/mesh), 10256 (kube-proxy metrics). We will send a full port list in the preflight.

Storage strategy
- Local NVMe for /var/lib/redwood/cache (ephemeral) with a 2x replicate snapshot to network-attached PVs for warm start.
- Persistent model artifacts: use a fast PV class backed by Ceph RBD (or iSCSI-backed LVM) with qos: high-iops. Archive tier to object store accessible only via private link — we can template a lifecycle policy for retention.
- PVC binding: use WaitForFirstConsumer for GPU pods to ensure PVs are scheduled to same rack when possible. Provide IO limits via Kubernetes CSI (iops/mbps).

Nodepool sizing notes (specific to your 8-GPU burst request)
- gpu-burst pool: start with 2 nodes x 4xA100-equivalent; autoscale to 4 nodes based on pending GPU-scheduled pods.
- cpu-worker pool: optimize for inference CPU workloads (packet processing + batching) with 96 vCPU / 384GB RAM per node baseline.

I'll draft a short mapping of StorageClass -> CSI parameters for your ops team to review. Also recommend a test plan for eviction scenarios (simulate NVMe loss for one rack).

—Karthik
Senior Technical PM, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: EdgeFusion on-prem cluster design review

Appreciate the detail. Two clarifications from our security & ops leads: 

1) Airgap/Offline install: we need an installer bundle that does not require outbound connections during bootstrap. The bundle must include container images, manifests, and a validated signature file. Can Redwood provide that and an offline verification script?

2) KMS: our HSM requires mTLS to the KMS endpoint and strict IP allowlisting; we cannot accept any key material that leaves our HSM. We need integration guidance for a customer-managed KMIP/HSM provider.

I've updated the storage-risk-register.xlsx with priority rows (attached). Notably: 
- Risk #3: NVMe degradation in rack A affects model warm caches — mitigation: cross-rack replication of last-good cache snapshot.
- Risk #7: Backup window for Ceph RBD conflicts with nightly maintenance window — mitigation: staggered snapshot schedule + SLO for restore time.

We can share rack inventory tomorrow. Also — we have an internal ticket: INF-4021 for proxy host provisioning; I will include the proxy host IPs in the preflight before Friday.

Attachments: storage-risk-register.xlsx

— Alex

- Provide final rack inventory + NVMe mapping (Alex / Priya) — due 2029-04-22.
- Share proxy host IP(s) for egress allowlist (Alex) — INF-4021 ticket.
- Confirm HSM/KMS connection details and certificate chain for mTLS (Priya) — due 2029-04-22.

Action items for Redwood (owners):
- Produce airgap bundle + offline verification script (Stephanie) — draft 2029-04-23.
- Deliver full port list + kernel/module checklist for preflight (Karthik) — 2029-04-22.
- Provide StorageClass -> CSI mapping and eviction test plan (Karthik / Marissa) — 2029-04-24.

On-site preflight: propose 2029-05-02 for a half-day workshop (ops + infra + security). Agenda will include: network routing decision, storage mapping, KMS integration walkthrough, and an evacuation test. Please confirm availability by EOD 2029-04-23.

We will version the manifests so you can pin the exact image set in the airgap bundle; DocuSign and procurement won't be blocked by the technical preflight but we'll add the required SOW language for HSM integration.

Thanks again — we will treat NVMe degradation and the Ceph backup window as high-priority items in the risk register. Marissa — can you draft the mutual action plan doc after Karthik's StorageClass mapping? I'll circulate once reviewed.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
